records.question: In Attention Is All You Need (1706.03762v7), how many parallel attention layers (heads) h are used in the base Transformer model, and what are the query/key dimension d_k and model dimension d_model?
records.answer_text:
The base Transformer model uses 8 parallel attention heads, with query/key dimension d_k = 64 and model dimension d_model = 512. [Attention Is All You Need (arXiv:1706.03762v7), p.5, 3.2.2 Multi-Head Attention, In this work we employ h = 8 parallel attention layers, or heads. For each of these we use dk = dv = dmodel/h = 64., 1706.03762v7_s250_c0013]

Verified Citations:
- [Attention Is All You Need (arXiv:1706.03762v7), p.5, 3.2.2 Multi-Head Attention, In this work we employ h = 8 parallel attention layers, or heads. For each of these we use dk = dv = dmodel/h = 64., 1706.03762v7_s250_c0013]
records.reference_answer: The base Transformer uses h = 8 parallel attention layers (heads), d_k = d_v = 64, and d_model = 512 (Section 3.2.2, p. 5; Table 3, p. 9).

citations.claim_text: The base Transformer model uses 8 parallel attention heads, with query/key dimension d_k = 64 and model dimension d_model = 512.
citations.locator_detail: In this work we employ h = 8 parallel attention layers, or heads. For each of these we use dk = dv = dmodel/h = 64.

records.question: What value of label smoothing (epsilon_ls) was used during training in Attention Is All You Need, and how did it affect perplexity and BLEU score?
records.answer_text:
The Transformer model used label smoothing with εls = 0.1, which increased perplexity but improved accuracy and BLEU score. [Attention Is All You Need (arXiv:1706.03762v7), p.8, 5.4 Regularization, Label Smoothing During training, we employed label smoothing of value ϵls = 0.1 [36]. This hurts perplexity, as the model learns to be more unsure, but improves accuracy and BLEU score., 1706.03762v7_s250_c0023]

Verified Citations:
- [Attention Is All You Need (arXiv:1706.03762v7), p.8, 5.4 Regularization, Label Smoothing During training, we employed label smoothing of value ϵls = 0.1 [36]. This hurts perplexity, as the model learns to be more unsure, but improves accuracy and BLEU score., 1706.03762v7_s250_c0023]
records.reference_answer: Label smoothing of value epsilon_ls = 0.1 was applied; it hurts perplexity as the model learns to be more unsure, but improves accuracy and BLEU score (Section 5.4 Regularization, p. 8).

citations.claim_text: The Transformer model used label smoothing with εls = 0.1, which increased perplexity but improved accuracy and BLEU score.
citations.locator_detail: Label Smoothing During training, we employed label smoothing of value ϵls = 0.1 [36]. This hurts perplexity, as the model learns to be more unsure, but improves accuracy and BLEU score.

records.question: What is Inner Monologue in Moshi (2410.00037v1), and what is Moshi's theoretical latency versus achieved practical latency?
records.answer_text: Insufficient evidence in the research library: Unable to verify full factual and citation support.
records.reference_answer: Inner Monologue predicts time-aligned text tokens as a prefix to audio tokens, improving linguistic quality and enabling streaming ASR/TTS, with a theoretical latency of 160 ms and practical latency of 200 ms (Abstract, p. 1; Section 1, p. 2; Section 3.4, p. 12-14).

records.question: In the H-Net architecture (2507.07955v2), why does the encoder and decoder use Mamba-2 (SSM) layers while the main network uses Transformer layers?
records.answer_text: Insufficient evidence in the research library: Unable to verify full factual and citation support.
records.reference_answer: Mamba-2 (SSM) layers have stronger inductive biases and efficiency for fine-grained raw byte sequences in the outer encoder/decoder stages, while Transformer layers excel in the compressed main network once sequences are dynamically chunked into higher-level representations (Section 2.1, p. 4-5; Section 3.3, p. 18).

records.question: In the Moshi paper (2410.00037v1), what is the name of the text language model backbone, how many parameters does it have, and how many hours of unsupervised audio data were used in audio pre-training?
records.answer_text:
The text language model backbone used in Moshi is Helium. [Moshi (arXiv:2410.00037v1), p.8, 3.2 The Helium Text Language Model, Table 1: 7B‑parameter Helium language model, 2410.00037v1_s500_c0015] Helium has 7 billion parameters. [Moshi (arXiv:2410.00037v1), p.8, 3.2 The Helium Text Language Model, Table 1: 7B‑parameter Helium language model, 2410.00037v1_s500_c0015] Moshi was pre‑trained on 7 million hours of unsupervised audio data. [Moshi (arXiv:2410.00037v1), p.17, 4.2 Audio data, "We use a first audio collection of 7 million hours, which we call the unsupervised audio dataset", 2410.00037v1_s500_c0029]

Verified Citations:
- [Moshi (arXiv:2410.00037v1), p.8, 3.2 The Helium Text Language Model, Table 1: 7B‑parameter Helium language model, 2410.00037v1_s500_c0015]
- [Moshi (arXiv:2410.00037v1), p.17, 4.2 Audio data, "We use a first audio collection of 7 million hours, which we call the unsupervised audio dataset", 2410.00037v1_s500_c0029]
records.reference_answer: The text backbone is Helium, a 7B-parameter language model, and audio pre-training used 7 million hours of unsupervised audio content (Section 1, p. 2-3; Section 3.2, p. 7; Section 4.2, p. 17).

citations.claim_text: The text language model backbone used in Moshi is Helium.
Moshi was pre‑trained on 7 million hours of unsupervised audio data.

records.question: How does the RQ-Transformer in Moshi decompose sequence modeling into a Temporal Transformer and a Depth Transformer?
records.answer_text: Insufficient evidence in the research library: Unable to verify full factual and citation support.
records.reference_answer: The RQ-Transformer decomposes the flattened sequence of K residual audio codebooks across T timesteps into a large Temporal Transformer operating over the T timesteps and a smaller Depth Transformer predicting the K codebook tokens at each timestep (Section 3.4, p. 12-13, Figure 3).

records.question: What is the role of the Ratio Loss in Dynamic Chunking (2507.07955v2), and what happens during training without a target compression ratio constraint?
records.answer_text: Insufficient evidence in the research library: Unable to verify full factual and citation support.
records.reference_answer: The Ratio Loss regularizes the fraction of selected chunk boundaries toward a target compression ratio N, preventing the routing module from collapsing into the trivial solution of selecting every token as a boundary (no compression) (Section 2.2.3 Ratio Loss, p. 7-8).
